context.description: The encryption context: "default" sends {instance, purpose}; "off" sends none; an object is sent as is.

keyName.description: An alias such as alias/audit-seal (kms) or a transit key name. An ARN or a key id is refused.

keys.description: Where the keys live. Use `adapter` and a key by purpose (seal, pseudonym, conceal, archive), the shape of the storage port. Unset means no pseudonyms, no key material and no resolve.

adapter.description: The key service: `kms` (AWS KMS, keys by alias), `transit` (OpenBAO) or `local` (a root file; development).

archive.description: The key the archive's objects are encrypted with (for S3, the SSE-KMS alias).

conceal.description: The key identities are sealed under, for the cases the law requires them to be recoverable.

instance.description: Names the installation in the default encryption context ({instance, purpose}), so a ciphertext made for one installation does not open as another's under a shared key. Bound into ciphertexts: choose something stable and non-secret.

pseudonym.description: The key the per-tenant pseudonym secrets are wrapped under. Provisioned only for an installation that pseudonymises (the attested preset, or a profile that needs pseudonyms).

rootFile.description: The local adapter's root: a file of 32 bytes.

seal.description: The notary's seal key: asymmetric ECC P-384 (ES384). It signs; it takes no encryption context.

state.description: Where the wrapped per-tenant secrets behind the pseudonym purpose are kept, with the kms adapter: the index database (`backend: database`, through the process's own `database`; no SSM), or the installation's SSM Parameter Store (`backend: ssm`, under `root`/`address`). Nothing in it is usable without the pseudonym key.

address.description: With backend ssm, the key below the root, for example internal/pseudonym.

backend.description: `database` keeps them in the index database; `ssm` (the default, for a config that gives a root) in SSM Parameter Store.

root.description: With backend ssm, the SSM path prefix of the installation, for example /audit/main.

openbao.description: How a process reaches an OpenBAO transit engine: where it is, and exactly one way of signing in.

caFile.description: A PEM bundle trusted beside the system roots, for a server on a private chain.

login.description: Sign in with a JWT: the pod's projected service-account token, presented to an auth mount. Nothing is stored.

jwtFile.description: The file holding the JWT, read at every login because the kubelet replaces a projected token before it expires.

mount.description: The JWT auth mount, for example jwt-devel.
Where the transit engine is mounted.

namespace.description: The OpenBAO namespace the engine and the auth mount are in. Unset is the root namespace.

tokenFile.description: A file holding a token, read on every call, for a token something else keeps renewed.

tokenSecret.description: The NAME of the secret holding a token, resolved through `secrets`.

secrets.description: Where a field named `...Secret` finds the secret it names. One source for the whole file: `env` (the name is an environment variable), `file` (the name is a path under `root`, one file per secret: a mounted Kubernetes Secret) or `ssm` (the name is a SecureString under `root` in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, read with the process's own identity). On AWS Lambda use `ssm`: the function's environment is never a place for a secret. Unset is `env`.

signer.description: The key seals are signed with, a P-384 key (ES384). The private half should never be on the notary's disk: a managed key (`kms`) keeps it where the writer's role cannot reach it, which a `file` cannot.

file.description: A P-384 private key in a PEM file (PKCS#8 or SEC 1), for development.

kms.description: An AWS KMS key: ECC_NIST_P384, SIGN_VERIFY, signing ECDSA_SHA_384. The credentials are the SDK's ambient ones: in a cluster, the notary's Pod Identity or IRSA role, which is not the writer's.

key.description: The key's ARN, ID or alias.

region.description: The key's region, when it is not the SDK's.

sink.description: The writer this process records through: exactly one of `url` (a writer or receiver that serves the sink) and `sqs` (the ingest queue of a writer that runs elsewhere, such as the writer Lambda).

expect.description: What the writer at `url` is configured to give: `archived` for a writer, `queued` for a receiver in front of a queue, `logged` for one that only logs. A client cannot learn it until it writes, so the file says, and `require` is checked against it at start-up and against every acknowledgement afterwards. With `sqs` it is `queued`, which is all a queue gives, and may be left out.

sqs.description: The SQS queue a writer that runs elsewhere consumes: the process sends its records there and the acknowledgement is `queued`. The pod's identity needs `sqs:SendMessage` on it. Credentials are never in the file: the process uses the SDK's ambient ones, which on Kubernetes is the pod's workload identity (EKS Pod Identity or IRSA) bound through the service account.

fifo.description: The queue is FIFO. It must agree with the URL, which ends in `.fifo` for one. A FIFO queue absorbs a repeated record itself, inside its five-minute window; a standard queue relies on the writer's deduplication.

region.description: The queue's region. Unset is the SDK's: AWS_REGION, which EKS Pod Identity and IRSA set.

tokenFile.description: A file holding the token presented to the writer, read afresh on every request: in a cluster, the pod's projected service-account token. Unset presents none, which an anonymous trial install accepts. Not with `sqs`.

description: The configuration of `audit-notary --config`, which seals the hours of the archive: one signed seal per profile, tenant and hour, chained through `prev`. Secrets are never in this file: a field named ...Secret holds the NAME of a secret, which the `secrets` block says how to find (an environment variable, a file or an SSM parameter). Telemetry is the OTEL_* environment, not configuration.

apiVersion.description: The version of this document's shape, `audit.truvity.github.io/audit-notary/v2`. Absent means version 1, which is deprecated and read for one minor (`truvity.github.io/audit-notary/v1`); another value is refused, so that a later shape arrives by a version and not by a file that quietly means something else.

archive.description: What the process adds to the deployment's presets: where their credentials are read from, and the default key.

ca.description: A bundle of certificate authorities, for a store whose certificate is not signed by a public root.

kmsKey.description: The key objects are encrypted with where a preset names no `key_alias` of its own. Unset uses the bucket's default encryption, which a deployment should still be setting.

sluisDir.description: The directory a secrets operator projects the documents a preset's `credentials_ref` names into: the document is read at `<sluisDir>/<credentials_ref>`, and read again when it changes and before the credential expires. Mount the Secret as a directory, not with subPath, so the file follows the rotation. Exclusive with `sluisRoot`.

sluisRoot.description: The SSM root of the secret store of the sluis installation that rotates a preset's `credentials_ref` (`/sluis/<instance>`). The document is read at `<sluisRoot>/<credentials_ref>` with the process's own identity, and read again before the credential expires. Exclusive with `sluisDir`; needed when a preset names `credentials_ref` and the process reads SSM.

stateRoot.description: The root of the installation's state store (SSM Parameter Store, through the storage port), for example /audit/main. A preset's `credentials` address in the deployment document is read below it with the process's own identity: the value is a JSON object {accessKeyID, secretAccessKey}. No secret is in this file. Needed when a preset names `credentials`.

deployment.description: Path to the profile configuration. Its `presets` are the stores seals are put in, each profile's in the store of its preset.

keys.description: The seal key through the storage port: `keys.seal` names it, and the adapter says which service holds it. Exactly one of this and `signer`.

profiles.description: The profiles to seal. Unset seals every profile the archive has records for.

require.description: The weakest durability an acknowledgement from the writer may carry (`logged`, `queued` or `archived`). Unset checks nothing. Set, it needs `sink.expect` at least as strong, which is checked at start-up, and an acknowledgement weaker than this fails the write instead of passing it with a caveat. See ADR 0059.

settle.description: How long after an hour has ended it is sealed, so that a batch put late in the hour it is keyed by is in the seal. An hour is never sealed sooner.

signer.description: The seal key in the first releases' shape. Use `keys.seal`; exactly one of the two.

sink.description: The writer this job records what it sealed through (`audit.seal.written`).

title: audit-notary
